owner_posts.post_text:
A One Person Company is a way to run a business where one person is in charge, has limited liability, and the business is recognised as a company. This was started under the Companies Act, 2013, to help people who want to start a business on their own. 

Registering a One Person Company in India is especially good for people who work on their own, like freelancers, consultants and small business owners who want the protection of the law and to be seen as a company without needing partners.

This way of running a business combines the features of being a sole proprietor and a private limited company. It lets one person control the business while still having protection from losing personal money if the business faces problems. This means the owner’s personal assets are usually safe from business debts.

The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) is in charge of this in India. Everything is covered by their integrated system, from filing for incorporation to getting your company name approved. After that, your company is recognized by the law and is able to sign contracts, open bank accounts, and conduct business in accordance with corporate law.

High Court has delivered an important ruling clarifying when intellectual property disputes can bypass mandatory pre-institution mediation under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015.

🔍 What was the issue?
Whether a commercial suit alleging IP infringement can be filed directly without mediation when the plaintiff seeks urgent interim relief, even if there is a delay between discovery of infringement and filing the suit.

⚖️ What did the Court hold?
The Court reaffirmed that:
Pre-institution mediation is mandatory, unless the suit genuinely contemplates urgent interim relief.
In cases of continuing IP infringement, each infringing act gives rise to a fresh cause of action.
Delay alone does not defeat urgency if the infringement is ongoing.

💡 Why this matters:
This judgment strikes a critical balance between:
Encouraging ADR and mediation, and
Ensuring effective and timely protection of intellectual property rights.
It prevents procedural requirements from becoming barriers in cases of persistent commercial harm, while safeguarding against misuse of “urgency” as a tactic to bypass mediation.

🔑 Legal takeaway:
In IP infringement cases, exemption from pre-institution mediation is available even after delay, if the plaintiff shows a continuing wrong and genuine need for urgent relief.
